grammar.title: The Future Tense (Futuro Semplice) for Plans and Formal Communication
grammar.explanation: The future tense in Italian is formed by modifying the infinitive ending: -are verbs change -are to -er, then add: -ò, -ai, -à, -emo, -ete, -anno. For -ere and -ire verbs, drop the final -e and add the same endings. Irregular stems include: avere -> avr-, essere -> sar-, andare -> andr-, fare -> far-, potere -> potr-. In formal business Italian, the future is preferred over the present for plans: 'Invierò il rapporto domani' (I will send the report tomorrow).
